title: Lock out a named miniature breaker with a spring-pin lockout, two hands, and a padlock
instruction: Lock out the breaker with the blue label: hold the red lockout by its body with one hand and press and hold its black button with the other, push it onto the breaker's switch, then let go of the button so its pins catch. Put the padlock's shackle through the hole in the lockout's stem and snap it shut. Leave the other breakers as they are.
context: Before work on a circuit its breaker is locked OFF with a lockout and a personal padlock. A pin-out lockout holds only if its pins are let go into the breaker's holes and the padlock then stops the button from being pressed again; one on the wrong breaker, or not set and padlocked, lets someone switch the circuit back on while a person is working on it.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top the bases stand on. Board: an off-white painted MDF back plate (30 cm wide, 29 cm tall, 1.2 cm thick) stands upright on the table and is fixed to it, its front face 37.2 cm in front of the bases, spanning 18 cm right to 12 cm left of the midline. A steel EN 60715 TS35 x 7.5 DIN rail (26 cm long) runs left-right across its face, centre 20.0 cm above the table. Breakers: five ABB S201-C16 single-pole miniature circuit breakers (2CDS251001R0164; 17.5 mm wide, 88 mm tall, 69 mm deep, grey plastic) clip side by side on the rail, the row centred 3 cm right of the midline, front faces 31.2 cm in front of the bases. Each has a coloured self-adhesive label (40 x 15.5 mm) flat on its top, 24.4 cm above the table, the label's centre 34.8 cm in front of the bases: from right to left blue (breaker centre 6.5 cm right of the midline), yellow (4.75 cm right), green (3 cm right), white (1.25 cm right), orange (0.5 cm left). The blue breaker's toggle is OFF (down); the other four are ON (up). Lockout: a Brady pin-out miniature circuit breaker lockout of the push-button, spring-pin type (as Brady 090844: red plastic body 20 mm across with a 24.1 mm flange at its outer end and a black nose at its breaker end; a black oval push button (9 x 24 mm) on a flat stem standing 13 mm out from the flange when released, with a 7.1 mm padlock hole across the stem; two steel wire pins, one above and one below the nose's toggle pocket, hooked ends pointing toward each other, that swing outward only while the button is held in), lies on a grey plastic post (1.4 x 0.8 cm, 15.6 cm tall, on a 6 x 5 x 1 cm foot) whose centre is 25.5 cm in front of the bases and 16 cm right of the midline. The lockout is centred on the post with its axis pointing forward, 16.7 cm above the table, its open (pin) end toward the board and its button toward the robot. Each breaker has two pin holes in its front face, one 8 to 13.5 mm above and one 8 to 13.5 mm below the toggle's centre line (4 mm wide), with a 3 mm face wall the pins hook behind. Padlock: a Master Lock 410 Zenex safety padlock (purple, 410PRP; thermoplastic body 38 mm wide, 45 mm tall, 19 mm thick; 6.35 mm steel shackle with 38 mm vertical and 20 mm horizontal clearance; 0.10 kg), unlocked with its shackle popped up 16 mm, stands upright on a grey plastic column (3.0 x 0.9 cm, 14.6 cm tall, on a 6 x 5 x 1 cm foot) 26.5 cm in front of the bases and 8.5 cm left of the midline. Its body's width runs forward, so the two shackle legs are one behind the other, the free (short) leg farther from the robot. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. Nothing else is on the table. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if, before the after-release check, at any time: the lockout is set on, or rests pushed onto for 0.5 s or more, any breaker other than the blue one; any other breaker's toggle moves 2 mm or more at its tip; or the blue breaker's toggle reaches ON. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if the lockout is pushed fully onto the blue breaker's toggle (its nose within 2 mm of the breaker's face, its axis within 2 mm of the toggle's centre line, tilted under 8 degrees); 0.5 if it is also set there (button let go: out more than 65% of its 13 mm travel, and both pins swung back in, hooked behind the holes' edges); 0.75 if the padlock's short leg also passes through the hole in the lockout's stem; 1.0 if the padlock is also shut (shackle latched) through that hole and the after-release check passes. After-release check, done by the reviewer once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the lockout and padlock for 1 s, with a push-pull spring scale: (1) press the button straight toward the board at 20 N for 1 s; pass if it goes in less than half its travel (6.5 mm); (2) keep pressing it at 20 N and pull the lockout's flange straight away from the board at 20 N for 1.5 s; pass if the lockout moves less than 3 mm; (3) push the lockout's body upward (toward ON) at 10 N for 1 s; pass if it moves less than 3 mm and the blue breaker stays OFF (its toggle short of the middle of its travel). All three must pass for 1.0; a shut padlock that fails any of them scores 0.75. Distances are read with a rule or from a photo with a scale in view.
reset_notes: Open the padlock with its key and take it off the stem; press and hold the lockout's button so the pins swing out and pull the lockout off; check the blue breaker is OFF and the other four ON; put the lockout back on its post (axis forward, button toward the robot) and the open padlock back on its column with its short leg toward the board. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies, box colliders, station arm gains. Geometry holds the lockout: the pins' feet sit behind the holes' edges, the pocket blocks the toggle, the shackle in the stem stops the button. The button-to-pin cam is a PhysX mimic joint; toggle detent and padlock latch are rules. Hole sizes, button spring (1.2-3.2 N) and check forces are our choice. The after-release check is applied in the simulator after the recording. Details in the README.
scores: Dream-1 run: not scored (the official Dream client stopped the trial at step 2,097 with PolicyError: a gripper command of -0.051, outside 0..1; up to then neither arm had touched the lockout or the padlock, so it would have scored 0); demo: 1.0
